title: fix(spec,runtime): bind the package-install contract to the door that serves, and honour enableOnInstall
body:
Fixes #18058

Clause-②: yes

Ruling: batch #148 item 4, letter **A**, maintainer 「同意」 2026-09-17T14:27Z (issue comment `5716042643`). Scope = **what the live door accepts today**. Options B, C and D were ruled out by name, and no new install option is designed here.

## The defect

`PackageInstallRequestSchema` was declared, published and bound to `POST /api/v1/packages/install` — a path the composed runtime mounts nowhere — while `POST /api/v1/packages`, the door that actually answers `201`, had no declared request contract at all. The read contract was strictly more truthful than the write contract producing the rows it describes, and three shapes were silent because of it: an undeclared `overwrite`, a declared-and-unhonoured `enableOnInstall`, and a published README example that cannot parse.

## What this PR does

| Ruling clause | What landed |
|:---|:---|
| Bind the contract to `POST /api/v1/packages`; remove the phantom binding | `PackageApiContracts.installPackage.path` is now `/api/v1/packages`; the module route table, the section heading and the `@example` follow. No published route row named the phantom (see M1). |
| Declare `overwrite`, and the door must **honour** it | `PackageInstallRequestSchema.overwrite?: boolean`. The honour half was already true and is now measured and pinned (M2) — the missing half was the declaration. |
| Decide the bare-manifest body form by measurement | **Kept.** New `PackageInstallBodySchema` = a union of the wrapped request and a bare `ManifestSchema` — two DISJOINT forms, of which only the bare one is closed. ⚠️ Corrected after the at-tier review (record `5720011982`, F3): `PackageInstallRequestSchema` is a `z.object` in strip mode, so the WRAPPED branch is not closed — `{ manifest: SDK, bogus: 1 }` is accepted and `bogus` silently dropped. ⛔ It is deliberately NOT made `.strict()`: that would refuse bodies the door serves today. (M3) |
| Name the manifest STAGE the way the read side does | The `manifest` slot is named as the **AUTHORING** stage in its declaration, its `.describe()` and the doc block, with the asymmetry against `InstalledPackageAtEitherStageSchema` stated: the read doors are reached at two stages, this wire at one. |
| `enableOnInstall`: honour it or remove its three declarations | **Honoured** at the live door. It is a one-PR fix and needs **no new engine capability** (M4), so the stop-and-report condition did not fire. No fourth declaration was added. |
| The README example and the SDK's pinned call must parse green | Both do, and both are pinned (M5). The README example as it shipped is pinned **red** so the fixture cannot go vacuous. |

## Measurements

Every exit code below was captured after a redirect, never through a pipe. Every zero reading carries a same-subject lit control that HITS, plus a dark control.

**M1 — the phantom path is served by nothing.** `git grep -l "packages/install"` at the merge base `62bce5c297` resolves in **3** files: `packages/spec/src/api/package-api.zod.ts`, its own test, and the auto-generated `content/docs/references/api/package-api.mdx` (EXIT=0). LIT control, same instrument, same subject shape — `packages/publish` — resolves in **45** files including mounted-route source (`packages/rest/src/package-routes.ts`, `rest-route-ledger.ts`); DARK control `packages/zzznosuchroute` resolves in 0, EXIT=1. Source reading agrees: `handlePackagesRequest` branches on `parts.length === 0` (GET/POST), `=== 1` (GET/PATCH/DELETE), `=== 2` and `=== 4` — there is **no one-segment POST branch**, so `/packages/install` falls through unhandled, and `packages/rest`'s registrar mounts only `POST /api/v1/packages/publish`. `check:route-envelope` EXIT=0 and `check:route-ledger-census` EXIT=0 after the rebind.

**M2 — `overwrite` was honoured and undeclared, which is the wrong half to be missing.** `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` reads `body?.overwrite === true || query?.overwrite === 'true' || query?.overwrite === true` and gates the 409 duplicate-id guard on it, so the ruling's "honour it, not merely accept it" is satisfied by measurement rather than by new code. Exact-word `git grep -cw overwrite` on `package-api.zod.ts` at the merge base = **0**, EXIT=1. LIT control, same exact word, same instrument, over `packages/spec/src/**/*.ts` = **23** files, EXIT=0 ⇒ the word is alive in that tree and the zero is a real absence on this subject. DARK control = 0, EXIT=1. A loose substring grep is a dud here — it matches `overwriteExisting` and friends — so exact-word matching was used throughout.

**M3 — first-party callers post a bare manifest FORM; their CONTENT is a different question.** ⚠️ **Corrected after the at-tier review (record `5720011982`, F2), which falsified this section as originally written.** The door reads `const manifest = body.manifest || body`, and two drives do exercise it with no wrapper: `packages/runtime/src/package-door-namespace-conflict-code.test.ts` posts `{ id, name: id, namespace, version }` and `packages/runtime/src/domain-handler-registry.test.ts:582` posts `{ id: 'pkg-a', name: 'A' }` — both re-read on the current tree. ⭐ But the review MEASURED that the bodies those two actually send are **REFUSED** by the new `PackageInstallBodySchema` (`invalid_union`), so they establish that the bare FORM is driven, ⛔ not that their content parses. The original claim here — that these two are evidence the bare content must be kept — was wrong, and the fixture that said it posts "exactly this" carried an extra `type: 'app'`, the very key that decides the parse. The form is kept and declared, as the ruling directs; the residual content classes are enumerated in the docblock and the changeset.

**M4 — honouring `enableOnInstall` is a one-PR fix with no new engine capability.** Readers in the three handler packages at the merge base: `git grep -lw enableOnInstall -- packages/runtime packages/metadata-protocol packages/objectql` = **0** files, EXIT=1; LIT control, same instrument and the same three trees, `overwrite` = **40** files, EXIT=0 ⇒ the instrument reaches those handler trees. Declarations found: three Zod field sites (`api/package-api.zod.ts:261`, `kernel/package-registry.zod.ts:283`, `marketplace/marketplace.zod.ts:494`) plus one TypeScript interface field (`contracts/package-service.ts:46`) — the ruling's "three declarations" are the three Zod ones. The capability the door needs already exists and was already imported into this very file for `PATCH /packages/:id/disable`: `SchemaRegistry.disablePackage(id)` (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:4328`) and `setPackageDisabled` (`packages/runtime/src/package-state-store.ts:168`, imported at `packages.ts:85`). So honouring is two existing calls, not a new seam.

**M5 — the two acceptance fixtures.** The README example as shipped is refused on three counts (no `id`, no `type`, and a `label` key the closed manifest surface refuses by name) — and it also failed at the live door, which answered `400 Package id is required` for want of an `id`. So it is a documentation error, not traffic to accommodate: it is corrected, pinned green through the SDK's own wrapping, and its old text is pinned red. Both of the client SDK's pinned calls (`client.test.ts`, the `enableOnInstall` case and the `overwrite` case) parse green.

## Tests

New coverage, each slot failing without the change and passing with it:

- `packages/spec/src/api/package-api.test.ts` — the contract-map rebind, the whole map carrying no `/install` path, the bound input being the body schema, `overwrite` surviving a parse with its value intact, both body forms and their disjointness, the bare form refusing install options, both acceptance fixtures, and the manifest stage.
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-install-enable-on-install.test.ts` — ⚠️ **updated by the seat after the F1b round; the bullet as first written described this file at 9 tests and is superseded.** The file now carries **25** tests. `enableOnInstall: false` lands disabled in all three records (the returned row, the registry, the durable state file); for an **unseeded** id `true` and absent land enabled; the bare body form does **not** honour a key no schema declares there. The F1b block adds the cases that matter for the durable half: for an id the boot **seeded** disabled, `true` and absent land **disabled** and a restart REPLAYS the disable rather than undoing it, plus an 11-arm table (wrapped/bare, true/false/absent, fresh/overwrite, seeded/unseeded) measuring one invariant over every arm that reaches 201 — the state on disk is the state the door returned.

Suites — ⚠️ **this paragraph is the seat's, replacing a version pinned at a head three rounds back** (`os-dev.md:56` reserves the body to the PR-open write, so the round names the wording and the seat writes it). The fenced block below was run at `2dcce3e2c6` and is kept as the record of THAT round, ⛔ not as a claim about the current head.

At `0a02ad08d5f` (the F1b round): the runtime slot above ran 25/25 EXIT=0, and an independent at-tier review reproduced it and re-ran the one-line ablation at 8 failed / 17 passed. CI at that head: **33 success / 2 skipped / 0 failure**, all seven required contexts green. Earlier, at `14f9b00ccbd`: spec `test` 487 files / 14077, spec `test:repo` 31 / 536, spec `typecheck` EXIT=0; runtime `test` 267 files / 3696 passed + 1 skipped, runtime `test:repo` 2 / 69, runtime `typecheck` EXIT=0; client `test` 46 / 549, client `typecheck` EXIT=0 (`@objectstack/client` has no `test:repo` script — read from its `package.json`, not assumed).

⛔ **NOT MEASURED at the current head `26805a16da3`:** no suite was run there, and that is deliberate rather than an omission. That head's whole delta against `0a02ad08d5f` is **one markdown file under `.changeset`**, one insertion and one deletion, with no package in its dependency closure; the round declared the narrowing and ran the five gate families that actually read `.changeset` (the three changeset gates, the nul-byte gate and the fixed-roster gate), each after its own `--self-test`, each exit code captured by redirect and never through a pipe. CI's run at this head is the record for everything else.
```
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test        EXIT=0   486 files / 13964 tests passed
pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime test     EXIT=0   266 files /  3666 tests passed
pnpm --filter @objectstack/client test      EXIT=0    44 files /   535 tests passed
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck   EXIT=0
pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck EXIT=0
pnpm --filter @objectstack/client typecheck EXIT=0
npx eslint . --no-inline-config             EXIT=0   (repo-wide, not narrowed)
```

### Reverse verification

Both ablations mutate a committed file, prove the mutation reached disk by a hash that differs from the HEAD blob, run, and restore under a `trap ... EXIT INT TERM`. Neither subject resolves through a `dist/` — both are in-package source imports — so no rebuild leg applies.

- **Spec.** Restore `packages/spec/src/api/package-api.zod.ts` to the merge base. Anchors before/after: `overwrite: z.boolean().optional()` 1 to 0, `PackageInstallBodySchema` 5 to 0, `path: '/api/v1/packages/install'` 0 to 1. Suite EXIT=1, **14 failed / 42 passed**. Restored: `git diff HEAD --stat` empty, `git status --porcelain` empty, on-disk hash `9af3a3aba8` equals the HEAD blob.
- **Runtime.** Restore `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` to the merge base. Anchors before/after: `body?.enableOnInstall === false` 1 to 0, `const wrapped = manifest !== body` 1 to 0. Suite EXIT=1, **2 failed / 3 passed** — and the two that failed are exactly the two `enableOnInstall: false` cases, while the `true`, absent and bare-form cases stayed green, which is what says the pins are about the honour path and not about installing at all. Restored: on-disk hash `8717e40257` equals the HEAD blob.

Direction in both cases was **turns red**, as predicted before running.

### Gates

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` EXIT=0 — all 15 generated artifacts up to date after regenerating the four this diff proved stale (`api-surface`, `export-origins`, `declaration-map`, `content/docs/references/**`); `authorable-surface` and the JSON-schema manifest were regenerated by the build. Every surface diff is purely additive: `PackageInstallBody{,Parsed,Schema}` added, `PackageInstallRequest:overwrite` added, nothing removed or narrowed.

Also green, each captured by redirect: `check:adr-0087-registration --base origin/main`, `check:changeset-no-major --base origin/main`, `check:empty-changeset --base origin/main`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:route-envelope`, `check:route-ledger-census`, `check:published-readme-links`, `check:published-files`, `check:doc-anchors`, `check:docs-single-h1`, `check:docs-spec-enumerations`, `check:quick-reference-counts`, `check:pm-widening-tells`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:spec-parsed-alias`, `check:objectui-changeset`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:doc-frontmatter`, `check:docs-section-name`, `check:spec-docblock-symbol-anchors`, `check:undeclared-dep-imports`, `check:doc-route-spelling --advisory`.

**NOT MEASURED — `pnpm check:published-readme-exports`, exit 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET).** It needs every published package built and 19 are not built in this worktree; exit 3 is that gate's own distinct "nothing was measured" code, not a finding. It is not among the 107 families `dispatch-gates` derives for this diff — it is an artifact-roster family — and CI builds fresh. The rest of the 107 are CI's lap.

## Acceptance notes

Noted while measuring, deliberately not fixed here and not filed:

- The three near-duplicate install-request declarations — `PackageInstallRequestSchema` (api), `InstallPackageRequestSchema` (`kernel/package-registry.zod.ts`) and the marketplace one — still differ only in `artifactRef`. This PR touched the first and left the other two alone, because the ruling's scope is the live HTTP door and the other two are other surfaces' contracts. Carrier: whichever PR next has to choose among them. Carrier if that never happens: none.
- `enableOnInstall` is still declared on two other schemas (`kernel/package-registry.zod.ts:283`, `marketplace/marketplace.zod.ts:494`) whose own doors this PR did not measure. The ruling's honour-or-remove applies to the install door, which now honours it; whether those two doors honour theirs is a separate measurement on a separate surface. Carrier: a card about those doors, if one is ever opened. Carrier today: none.
- `platformVersion` and `artifactRef` are declared on the install request and read by no handler at the live door. They are the same shape as the `enableOnInstall` defect and were left untouched because the ruling names `enableOnInstall` and forbids widening the scope; they are named here so the next reader does not have to re-measure. Carrier: this note.
- #17536 remains open and is not addressed here; #17518 and #17535 were not touched.
